indication_area: Autoinflammatory and rheumatic disease (rheumatoid arthritis, CAPS/NOMID, Still's disease, FMF; IL-1 blockade)
revenue_scope: Worldwide Kineret product revenue as recorded by Sobi (its 'Kineret' / 'Inflammation: Kineret' line), SEK
moa: recombinant human interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (blocks IL-1 alpha and beta)

approval_evidence.quote: Kineret (anakinra) for injection, for subcutaneous use ... Initial U.S. Approval: 2001

series_start_reason: First full quarter of Biovitrum's ownership of the Kineret license, not the launch (Kineret was approved in the U.S. in 2001 and sold by Amgen before this series). Biovitrum acquired the global Kineret license from Amgen on 2008-12-15 and its Full Year Report 2008 names Kineret only as an acquired product, with the 2008 comparative columns of the 2009 reports printing 25.8 for the 2008-12-15 to 2008-12-31 stub, which is not a full quarter and is not used. Before the acquisition Biovitrum reported Kineret only as Nordic co-promotion revenue (a different scope). Amgen printed worldwide Kineret sales only as full years (2001 and 2002) and nothing for 2003-2008. No launch quarter is cited.
notes: Currency SEK (millions). The 2011-2017 quarters print one decimal until 2014 and integers after. Sobi's reports in this span show Kineret sales in both Europe and North America (Q4 2012 report: 'growth in both North America and ...'); co-promotion revenue from Savient (2013) and Kineret-related royalty are separate lines and are not in the Kineret line. 2011Q4 comes from the prior-year column of the Q4 2012 report because the Q4 2011 report prints only the full year. 2018Q4, 2019Q1 and 2019Q2 are read from the quarter's own results presentation (Kineret slide: 'Q4 revenue SEK 335 M', 'Revenues of SEK 346 M', 'Revenue of SEK 419 M') because the full-report PDFs of those quarters yielded no Kineret line under pdfplumber; 2019Q3-2020Q4 are read from the sobi.com report web pages (highlights text). Q4 sums vs full-year: 2011 421.9 vs printed 422.0; 2013 561.8 vs 561.7; 2014 609.4 vs 609.3; 2015 806 vs 805; 2018 1,319 vs 1,320 (Q4 2019 page); 2019 1,570 vs 1,571; 2020 2,080 vs 2,079; 2022 2,285 vs 2,284. All within rounding. 2012 quarters sum to 484.3 while the Q4 2012 report prints a full-year 484.7 (and a quarterly table showing Q4 as 130.6); the 0.4 difference is unexplained, so the full-year figure is not quoted on the 2012Q4 row. The series is continuous from 2009Q1. 2009Q1-2009Q3 are read from each quarter's own report, 2009Q4 from the full year report 2009 (2009 quarters sum 104.0 + 110.2 + 105.6 + 120.9 = 440.7, equal to the printed 440.7), 2010Q1 and 2010Q3 from each quarter's own report and 2010Q4 from the quarter's own results presentation (2010_Q4_sobi_presentation.pdf; the Q4 2010 report PDF's text layer groups the digits badly) (2010 quarters sum 104.6 + 113.0 + 103.4 + 101.3 = 422.3, equal to the printed 422.3). 2010Q2 is read from the prior-year column of the Q2 2011 report because the Q2 2010 report prints it as '113,0'. The 2010 reports restate some 2009 comparatives (for example Q4 2009 as 120.5 against the originally printed 120.9); each quarter here uses the figure as first printed. Amgen (prior owner) printed worldwide Kineret sales only as full years in its 10-K (2001: $12.3 million; 2002: $69.9 million) and no quarterly or later figure, so no Amgen quarters are joined.
search_log: Enumerated Sobi's financial-reports pages on sobi.com (listing page /en/financial-reports plus slug probes) for every quarter 2010Q1-2026Q2 and opened the 'Read full report' PDF of each; extracted every line containing Kineret with pdfplumber.

2018Q4-2020Q4 full reports have no text layer on the product pages (pdfplumber extracted no Kineret line from any of them): the sobi.com web page of each report was read instead; Q3 2019, Q4 2019, Q1-Q4 2020 pages print the quarter's own Kineret sales in the highlights text.

Q4 2018, Q1 2019 and Q2 2019 report web pages carry no Kineret figure; the quarter's own results presentation PDFs (2018_Q4_sobi_presentation.pdf, 2019_Q1_sobi_presentation.pdf, 2019_Q2_sobi_presentation.pdf) print it on the Kineret slide and were used.
Did not search for Amgen history or any other issuer that prints Kineret: Amgen is the licensor/manufacturer, not a seller after Sobi's takeover; not researched in this batch.

Extension (earlier quarters): opened every Sobi/Biovitrum report page from Q3 2006 to Q4 2010 on sobi.com and extracted Kineret lines with pdfplumber. Biovitrum reports before 2009 print Kineret only as Nordic co-promotion revenue (Q1 2009 report footnote: 'In 2008, until the time of the acquisition, the company reported sales of Kepivance and Kineret as co-promotion revenues. These revenues were generated exclusively by sales in the Nordic region.'); the Full Year Report 2008 dates the acquisition of Kineret to December 15th, 2008.

Quarters 2009Q1-2010Q4 read from the product tables of the 2009 and 2010 reports (URLs in the CSV); the Q2 2010 report prints '113,0' with comma decimals, so 2010Q2 comes from the Q2 2011 report's prior-year column (113.0); the Q4 2010 report PDF prints the Kineret line with broken digit grouping, so 2010Q4 is read from the Q4 2010 results presentation.

Amgen (CIK 318154) 10-Q, 10-K and 8-K earnings-release exhibits 2002-2009 scanned for Kineret with a figure: only the FY2002 10-K (filed 2003-03-10, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000089843003001854/d10k.htm) prints 'Worldwide Kineret sales for the years ended December 31, 2002 and 2001 were $69.9 million and $12.3 million'; no quarterly Kineret figure in any Amgen filing, so no earlier quarter exists and Amgen is not joined.
